frozen_candidate_root_contribution: A bounded, self-committed ABSTAINING — the deliberate holding-back of oneself from an activity one would otherwise engage in, sustained over a dedicated/consecrated span. The root contributes only the abstention/withholding-of-self vector; WHICH activity is withheld (eating/drinking/marital relations vs. speech) is supplied by context, not by the root.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: A bounded, self-committed ABSTAINING — the deliberate holding-back of oneself from an activity one would otherwise engage in, sustained over a dedicated/consecrated span. The root contributes only the abstention/withholding-of-self vector; WHICH activity is withheld (eating/drinking/marital relations vs. speech) is supplied by context, not by the root.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across the data the constant left after subtracting form and context is "deliberately withholding oneself from a normally-available activity for a set, dedicated period." The single most decisive occurrence is 19:26, where Mary declares "إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ... إِنسِيًّا" — here صَوْم is explicitly a vow of SILENCE (abstention from speaking), involving no food at all. This proves the root itself does not mean "not eating"; it means "abstaining/holding back," with the object of abstention being contextually filled (here, speech). The ritual occurrences then instantiate the same residue with a different object: 2:183 ٱلصِّيَامُ prescribed on believers; the two verbs 2:184 تَصُومُوا۟ and 2:185 فَلْيَصُمْهُ (perform the abstention / abstain through the month); 2:187 defines the temporal bounds of the abstention ("لَيْلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ... أَتِمُّوا۟ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيْلِ" — a daylight-bounded holding-back from food, drink, and رَفَث). The expiation cluster (2:196 صِيَامٍ / فَصِيَامُ, 4:92 فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ, 58:4 فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ, 5:89 فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ, 5:95 صِيَامًا) all present a bounded stretch of self-withholding offered as a substitute act. The active participle in 33:35 (ٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ) names people characterized by this habitual self-abstaining. Every form-family (verbal noun صوم/صيام, finite verb يصوم/تصوموا, participle صائم) and every sense-family (narrative vow of silence, prescribed Ramadan fast, juridical expiation, eschatological virtue) reduces to the same core: bounded, dedicated withholding-of-self.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: verbal noun صوم/صيام packages the abstention as a thing/state; finite verbs تَصُومُوا۟/يَصُمْ package it as an act performed; active participle صائم/صائمة packages it as an ascribed characteristic — none add semantic content beyond grammatical framing. CONSTRUCTION supplies the deontic/purpose vector, not the root: نَذَرْتُ ... صَوْمًا (vow/consecration frame, 19:26); كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ (prescription-upon, 2:183); فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ... (substitute/expiation frame, 2:196/4:92/58:4/5:89); temporal delimiters أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَٰتٍ, إِلَى ٱلَّيْلِ, شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ (the "bounded" span). PARTICIPANTS vary (Mary; the believing community; a killer/oath-breaker/ẓihār-offender/pilgrim/hunter). CONTEXT varies (Marian narrative, Ramadan law, kaffārah law, hajj, eschatological catalogue). Subtracting all four leaves the invariant: deliberate self-withholding from an otherwise-available activity for a dedicated bounded interval. Crucially, the varying object of abstention (speech vs. food/drink/relations) is a context layer, not a root feature — confirmed by the contrast between 19:26 and the ritual occurrences.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 19:26 (صَوْمًا = a vow of silence) is simultaneously the hardest case and the interpretive key. It is hardest because it superficially breaks the ritual-fast reading: no food, drink, or marital abstention is in view — the withheld activity is speech. But it reconciles perfectly with, and in fact establishes, the abstract residue: the root supplies "abstaining/holding-back," and the object of that abstaining is context-filled. Rather than being an anomaly, it is the internal evidence that forces the abstraction and rules out a food-specific core. It is fully reconciled by layer-subtraction (the object "speech" belongs to the context layer).
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is that the root denotes specifically "religious ritual fasting: abstaining from food, drink, and marital relations during daylight." This covers 13 of 14 occurrences smoothly. Internal evidence ARBITRATES DECISIVELY against it: 19:26 uses the same root صَوْم for a vow of silence with no ingestive component whatsoever, so a food-specific core is contradicted by the data itself. The generic "bounded self-withholding" reading survives 19:26 and equally covers the 13 ritual/juridical cases, so the internal data prefers the abstract residue. A second alternative — "consecration/dedication to God" — is refuted because dedication is contributed by the construction (نَذَرْت, كُتِب) and is absent as the invariant (the expiation cases foreground substitutive withholding, not consecration); the withholding element, not dedication, is what is present in all 14.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors: (1) عكف Ekf ('i'tikāf, devotional seclusion) — co-occurs in the very same verse 2:187 (عَٰكِفُونَ فِى ٱلْمَسَٰجِدِ); Ekf = staying-put / devoting one's PRESENCE to a place, whereas Swm = holding oneself BACK from an activity — presence vs. abstention. (2) صبر Sbr (patient endurance) — co-listed in 33:35 (ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ ... ٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ); Sbr = enduring an externally-imposed hardship, whereas Swm = voluntarily and deliberately renouncing a normally-permitted activity for a bounded span. (3) منع mnE / كفّ (withholding/preventing) — those typically withhold something from OTHERS, whereas Swm is reflexive self-withholding. Falsifiability: the reading fails if any occurrence used Swm for (a) merely enduring imposed adversity with no voluntary act of renunciation, (b) being devotionally present/adhering without any abstention, or (c) withholding a resource from another party rather than restraining oneself. No such occurrence appears in the 14.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — bounded, self-committed abstaining/withholding-of-self from a normally-available activity over a dedicated span — is surface-recoverable in every one of the 14 occurrences and across every form-family (verbal noun صوم/صيام, finite verbs تَصُومُوا۟/يَصُمْ, participle صائم/صائمة) and sense-family (Marian vow, Ramadan prescription, kaffārah substitution, hajj, eschatological virtue). The direction is determinate (agent restrains self from an activity) and the object of abstention is cleanly assignable to the context layer, not the root. The hardest case, 19:26, is not an anomaly but the internal disambiguator: applying صَوْم to a vow of silence proves the root abstracts away from food and refutes the narrower ritual-fast hypothesis on internal grounds alone. The contribution is sharply distinct from its co-textual neighbors عكف (presence-devotion) and صبر (endurance of imposed hardship). No occurrence resists the residue, so clean universal presence is honestly claimable; strength is STRONG rather than MODERATE because the invariant is directly present at the surface everywhere and requires no metaphorical bridge — only the recognition, itself internally attested, that the withheld object is context-supplied.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep of all 14 occurrences found NO genuinely failing occurrence; the core residue — bounded, dedicated withholding-of-self from a normally-available activity, with the WHICH-activity supplied by context — holds throughout. Hardest case, 19:26 (صَوْمًا), is the linchpin and it survives cleanly: Mary is told "فَكُلِى وَٱشْرَبِى" (eat and drink) immediately before vowing صوم, then "فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ... إِنسِيًّا" — proving the object of abstention here is SPEECH, not food. This is textual, not ad hoc, so the object-neutral bridge is non-circular. The 12 ritual/juridical occurrences (Ramadan fast 2:183/184/185; temporal bounds 2:187 ×2; expiation clusters 2:196 ×2, 4:92, 58:4, 5:89, 5:95; participle 33:35 ×2) all instantiate the same bounded self-withholding with the food/drink/رفث object contextually filled. Neighbor contrast holds: distinct from عكف (positive confinement-TO a place, notably co-occurring in 2:187 عَٰكِفُونَ), from صبر (endurance of imposed hardship, not renunciation of an available good), and from كفّ/إمساك (generic restraint lacking the consecrated bounded-span feature). Falsifiable — a صوم meaning motion/consumption or unbounded restraint would break it; none occurs. Two honest caveats that do NOT break any occurrence, so verdict remains SUPPORTED rather than downgraded: (1) the OBJECT-NEUTRALITY generalization is evidentially thin — 13 of 14 occurrences are the food/drink fast, so the claim that the root is indifferent to the withheld activity rests almost entirely on the single 19:26 case; it is decisive but singular. (2) The qualifier "self-committed" mildly over-specifies: 2:183 (كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ) and the kaffara occurrences are prescribed/imposed, not self-vowed like 19:26 (نَذَرْتُ); this is reconcilable only if "self-committed" is read reflexively as "self-directed holding-back-of-oneself" rather than "self-initiated by vow." Under that reading no occurrence is contradicted, hence no word_ref is listed as failing.

occurrence_dispositions.note: صَوْمًا paired with نَذَرْتُ ... فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ... إِنسِيًّا: an explicit vow of silence with no food involved. Residue = deliberate withholding-of-self over a dedicated span; object (speech) is contextually supplied. This is the anchor case for the root vector.
ٱلصِّيَامُ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ — prescribed self-abstention. Residue present; withheld activity (food/drink/relations) supplied by ritual context, not the root.
تَصُومُوا۟ over أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَٰتٍ — finite verb of performing the bounded abstention; residue directly recoverable.
فَلْيَصُمْهُ (abstain through the month of Ramadan) — dedicated, temporally bounded withholding-of-self; residue present.
أَتِمُّوا۟ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيْلِ — daylight-bounded holding-back from food/drink/رَفَث; explicit temporal bounds instantiate the residue.
لَيْلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ — the night belonging to the abstention period; verbal-noun designating the bounded self-withholding. Residue present.
فِدْيَةٌ مِّن صِيَامٍ — a stretch of self-abstention offered as juridical substitute (hajj expiation); residue recoverable as bounded withholding.
فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ — explicitly bounded (three days) substitute abstention; residue present.
ٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ — active participle naming men characterized by habitual self-abstaining as a virtue; residue present in the agent form.
ٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ — feminine participle of the same habitual self-abstaining virtue; residue present.
فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ — bounded, consecutive two-month self-withholding as expiation for accidental killing; residue present.
فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ — bounded consecutive abstention as ẓihār expiation; residue directly recoverable.
فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ — bounded three-day substitute abstention for oath-breaking; residue present.
عَدْلُ ذَٰلِكَ صِيَامًا — an equivalent measure of self-abstention as expiation for hunting in iḥrām; residue recoverable as bounded withholding.
